title: Release Conductor: Multi‑Arm Slice Heuristics (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
This scratchpad collects an opinionated set of heuristics for running multi-arm A/B (and multi-variant) rollouts across product + infra + SRE. The goal is pragmatic: give rollout stewards a compact checklist and a set of allocation/escape rules that work for low-latency LLM features where cost and latency tradeoffs are first-class.

Scope and assumptions:
- Feature surface: routing to model variants or quantization/latency tiers (hosted vs dedicated vs fallback).
- Traffic types: production user traffic + synthetic probes.
- We expect short-lived micro-experiments (hours→days) and longer cohort pilots (weeks).
- Primary signals: latency P50/P95/P99, cost per thousand tokens, quality deltas via prompt-set evals, error rate (5xx, model-timeouts), and human-reported regressions.

Core principles (short):
- Minimize blast radius: prefer many small slices over heavy-weight single-cohort changes.
- Signal orthogonality: separate latency/cost signals from quality signals; treat quality regressions as higher severity.
- Deterministic rollback windows: explicit window + automatic circuit-breakers.

Roles (quick):
- Release Conductor (owner): orchestrates traffic moves and monitors signals.
- Observability Lead: ensures dashboards + alerts are tuned.
- Model Steward: owns quality evals and human review.
- SRE: capacity & incident runway.

Allocation heuristics (multi‑arm):
1) Seed phase (0→1% total): 0.1–0.5% to each new arm, prefer isolated clients (employee, internal alpha). Run 1–4h.
2) Probe phase (1→5%): raise to 1% per-arm across multiple microcohorts; enable synthetic probes with identical prompt sets. Run 6–24h.
3) Confidence expansion (5→25%): move to stratified slices (geography, client tier, usage pattern). Increase only if: latency OK, cost delta within budget, no quality alerts. Run 24–72h.
4) Ramp (25→100%): staged doubling with monitoring gates every step. Use traffic-smoothing (ramp-up ramp-down windows) to avoid sudden thundering changes.

Multi-arm rebalancer (heuristic rules):
- Every control interval (10m): compute normalized z-scores for P95 latency, error-rate, and quality delta.
- If an arm exceeds 3σ on any safety signal → reduce that arm by 50% immediately and flag for human review.
- If an arm shows consistent +ve quality delta and neutral cost/latency for 6 consecutive intervals → double allocation (capped by global safety budget).
- If two arms conflict (one faster but worse quality): prefer quality unless latency exceeds SLA aggressively.

Safety gates and circuit-breakers:
- Latency SLO breach: automatic fallback to baseline variant for that slice if P95 > SLO * 1.25 for 3 consecutive intervals.
- Token-cost surge: if cost per 1k tokens increases > 30% and not justified by quality uplift → pause ramp and notify finance-gate.
- Behavioral regression: any human-reviewed critical regression → immediate global rollback to last stable model.

Observability checklist (dash + alerts):
- Per-arm time-series: requests, tokens, P50/P95/P99, error-rate, CPU/GPU utilization, cost per 1k tokens.
- Synthetic prompt-set pass/fail and top-10 failing prompts.
- Drift monitor: distribution shift on prompt length, top tokens, response length.
- Customer-facing telemetry: per-route latency and error SLA.
- Alert thresholds: page on infra OOMs, page on model-timeout spikes, slack-only for minor quality deltas.

Rollout runbook (quick play):
- Pre-launch: confirm canary config + steady-state synthetic baseline recorded, blockers cleared, stakeholders present.
- Launch seed: allocate seed arms, start synthetic runner, hand-off to Observability Lead.
- 10m loops: Reconciler computes gates; steward approves or pauses.
- Escalation: if circuit-breaker trips, SRE triages infra, Model Steward investigates prompt-level failures.
- Post-mortem: if rollback occurs, capture causal chain + ticket for mitigations within 48h.

Edge/error modes we've seen (notes):
- Oscillation: frequent small ramps cause sampling noise to trigger rebalances—introduce dampening factor (momentum) in allocator.
- Cohort contamination: cross-cohort caching caused spillover of cached prefixes—ensure KV cache keys include cohort id for experiments.
- Cost-heat from hallucination loops: longer generations causing runaway tokens—add hard token caps for experimental arms.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Can we safely use adaptive allocation (bandit-style) for quality-limited features while preserving audit trails? Need a short POC with constrained arms.
- How aggressive should cost gates be for enterprise vs freemium tiers? Proposal: tiered budgets per-customer class.
- Should we instrument per-user risk scores and exclude high-risk users from experiments by default?

Action items (owners):
- Observability: add per-arm synthetic prompt top-10 failure view (Marco) — due 2026-01-20.
- Infra: KV cache cohort-keying change (Noah) — due 2026-01-18.
- Product: draft escalation matrix for quality vs latency tradeoffs (Aisha) — due 2026-01-22.

Notes to self / quick heuristics to remember:
- Always bias early allocations to internal + low-risk cohorts.
- Keep synthetic prompt runner in the loop—often earliest failure signal.
- Automate simple reverts; reserve manual rollout for ambiguous quality issues.

References / links: CONFLUENCE-8572 (runbooks), JIRA-MLSERV-4321 (allocator spike), github.com/redwood-inference/release-orchestra/pull/89 (prototype rebalancer).

End of scratchpad (will fold into a formal playbook once POC results land).
